_doc: Humanoid animation metadata (ADR 0004). Times are seconds into the source clip. Action clips play the section [start, end] rate-scaled so `contact` lands on the caller's data time (an attack's windup): rate = (contact - start) / windup, capped at max_rate by trimming the lead-in instead of slowing the hit. A clip is REAL when an animation of that name exists in a rig's glb (merged by tools/art/blender_process.py from the manifest's anims) and PROCEDURAL otherwise (HumanoidOverlays on the idle base pose). Real always outranks procedural, so dropping a real clip in under the same name needs no code change: give it top-level start/contact/end here (defaults: the whole clip, contact = start). The `procedural` block holds the overlay's own timing and is used only while the overlay is what plays. `aliases` map the game's clip vocabulary onto humanoid clips, best first; the game name itself is always tried before its aliases (a real `stagger` beats the `hit` fallback). `mannequin_contact` is the legacy 17-bone rig's contact fraction of its 1-second clips.

_doc_carry: models.<id>.carry names a looping clip played on the arms only (HumanoidRig upper layer) whenever no action owns the rig, so a held two-handed weapon stays in the hands while the legs walk.

weapon_class._doc: weapon kit -> clip set (clip_sets) and grip (mounts weapon@<class>)

clip_sets._doc: weapon class -> game clip name -> library clips, best first (HumanoidLib.candidates). `_all` answers for every class. Only models with clip_sets: true use them. `_carry` names a looping arms-only clip that holds a two-handed weapon through locomotion (HumanoidRig carry layer).

polish._doc: strike polish layered over the clips by CharVisual (humanoids only): a lean away through the wind-up, spent by the contact frame, and a forward dig on a landed hit that Juice's hit-stop holds. Degrees and seconds. trail_lead: seconds before the hit window opens that the swing ribbon starts drawing.

_doc_borrow: models.<id>.borrow names another model whose own sectioned clips (its `clips` rows: the Bearer's drink, rest, ...) this model plays as its own, with the same sections. The Bearer's outfits borrow bearer_traveller's, so every outfit drinks and kneels alike.
